title: Wafer Geometry Measurement - CD Variation Detection on Surfscan SP7
subtitle: Post-Etch Quality Validation for 7nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Anna Petrova

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP7 system to detect and classify CD Variation defects during post-etch inspection at the 7nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for CD Variation defects that are critical to yield at the 7nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP7 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP7
- Inspection Type: Wafer Geometry Measurement
- Target Defect: CD Variation
- Process Step: Post-Etch
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 7nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP7 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-etch monitoring in the 7nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP7
Software Version: v11.5.443
Recipe: WAFER_GEOMETRY_MEASUREMENT_7nm_POST_ETCH
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (138 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP7 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Wafer Geometry Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target CD Variation defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 7nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 77 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 94% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.8% for Wafer Geometry Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.99 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-01-18
Wafers Tested: 14
Total Defects Found: 201
Defect Density: 63.98 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.5%
Capture Rate: 88.5%
Test Duration: 125 minutes
System Uptime: 97.8%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP7 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting CD Variation at the 7nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for CD Variation at 7nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
